spec_match.rationale: The element set, attributes and command vocabulary were read from WHATWG HTML PR 12011, and then every claim was checked against the browser rather than repeated from the draft. That is how the build found that Chrome's implementation is partial in a specific way: the elements and the invoker plumbing are in, while type, fieldset checkable, show-menu and hide-menu are not. The demos say so.

interactive.rationale: An element inventory with a live prototype browser and an attribute reflection table; a working three-menu application whose menus open through command=toggle-menu with no script involved in opening them, plus a live command log; and a state page with a per-keyword command prober, a free-text keyword input, and working checkbox and radio items.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index frames the feature as giving the platform an actual menu, in contrast to <menu>, which is a list with a misleading name — the proposal's own framing. Each card describes what its page does.

edge_cases.rationale: The unknown-element fallback is a first-class case: it is measured, and the measurement corrected a claim this build had already written. Also covered: unrecognised command keywords reflecting as the empty string, the two-dash rule and the reserved undashed namespace, commandfor resolving only inside a document, and a disabled item.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5206029088063488 on the index and all three concept pages, with the WHATWG pull request, the Open UI explainer and MDN's invoker commands page.

conformance.rationale: Seven immutable assertions: the three interfaces, menulist hidden by user-agent style, command/commandfor reflection including the element reference, unknown keywords reflecting empty, the two-dash custom command rule, and the end-to-end claim — a menuitem opening its menulist into the top layer with no popover attribute anywhere.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150, twice: flag off (3/3, 28 assertions — all three tags are HTMLUnknownElement, nothing reflects, clicking an item sends nothing) and with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features (3/3, 28 assertions — all three interfaces present, menulist display:none, clicking the File title opens the menulist and matches :popover-open, clicking New delivers --doc-new to the document and changes it).

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert carrying whether the elements are known, how many attributes reflect, how many pieces of the state model are present, and each command received.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px minimums on the inputs and 34–36px on menu rows where a denser menu is the correct affordance, and every wide table in its own scroll container.

accessibility.rationale: The stateful items carry role=menuitemcheckbox / menuitemradio and aria-checked written by this page, because the type attribute that would let the browser supply them is not implemented here — the page says that in the note rather than letting it look automatic. What has NOT been verified is the implicit accessibility mapping of menubar/menulist/menuitem themselves: element.role reflects the attribute, not the computed role, so reading it proves nothing and the demos do not claim it.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The application shell and menus use flex with wrapping; the inventory and vocabulary tables scroll inside their own containers; the menubar row wraps rather than overflowing at 360px.

openQuestions.title: Verify the implicit ARIA roles from the accessibility tree
openQuestions.detail: The central claim of the proposal is that these elements are exposed as a menu without any role attributes, and this build cannot check it: element.role reflects the content attribute, and there is no DOM API for the computed role. It needs the accessibility tree — chrome-devtools-mcp, or a CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree call the drive harness does not currently make. Until then the demos state the elements' purpose and do not assert their roles.

openQuestions.title: Keyboard behaviour is described, not measured
openQuestions.detail: Arrow-key movement between items and between menus, typeahead, and Escape closing the right layer are the reason to use these elements over divs, and the a-real-menubar page invites the reader to try them without asserting an outcome. Synthesised key events would not settle it either, since the behaviour lives in the browser's own event handling. This needs trusted input dispatch through CDP.

openQuestions.title: Re-check when type and fieldset checkable land
openQuestions.detail: The commands-and-state page implements checkbox and radio behaviour in its own script and says so plainly. When the type attribute and fieldset checkable arrive, that script becomes exactly the code the proposal exists to delete — and the page should delete it, keeping the gap table as the record of what changed.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle a popover from a button without javascript invoker commands
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use command/commandfor invoker attributes to open and close overlays declaratively rather than wiring click handlers, and let the platform own focus and dismissal.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The menu bar opens its menus entirely through command="toggle-menu" commandfor="…"; the page's only listener is a single command handler on the document being edited, and it never touches a menu element.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Measured: with the elements known, clicking the File title makes its menulist match :popover-open with no script involved.

guidanceConsulted.query: menu with checkbox and radio items accessible names and state
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Expose stateful menu items with the right role and a live checked state, and keep every item keyboard-operable.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied by hand — role=menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio, aria-checked kept in sync, Enter and Space handled, tabindex on the items — precisely because the type attribute that would supply this is not implemented here. The page says the ARIA is its own rather than the browser's; when type lands, this becomes removable.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive toggles the checkbox and asserts both the checked attribute and aria-checked; it selects a radio and asserts exactly one stays checked.

guidanceConsulted.query: graceful fallback for an unknown html element
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Unknown elements are inert and inline; design so the markup degrades to something readable rather than something broken or hidden.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The fallback is measured and reported on the page: without the elements every menu renders as inline text, and — the part that matters — clicking an item sends no command, because command/commandfor belong to specific elements rather than to any element that spells them. The page states the consequence for anyone shipping this today.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Flag-off drive run: zero log lines and unchanged status after clicking a menu item.

summary: Three concepts about an element set that is half-landed, built to say exactly which half. The elements, the user-agent styling and the invoker plumbing are real and demonstrated end to end; the state model is not, and the page that would use it implements the behaviour itself and labels it as its own work. The implicit ARIA roles — the proposal's central promise — remain unverified and are recorded as the top open question rather than asserted.
